question.question: After a committed JointImplicit change is applied while a leadership transfer is active, does Raft retain or regenerate the automatic joint-exit work when the transfer times out and the original leader continues with a responsive joint quorum but no new client proposals?
question.importance: A missed automatic exit can retain outgoing voters indefinitely and prevent later membership changes; it can make continued availability depend on participants intended to leave. This is a potential membership-progress defect, not an observed safety violation.
objects: f-membership active joint configuration and AutoLeave
contexts: Stable leader term with JointImplicit membership
Transfer initiated after entry commitment but before application completion
Transfer target unavailable; remaining quorum processes messages and storage
No unrelated proposals or forced election after transfer timeout
event_paths: Commit JointImplicit entry -> initiate transfer -> ApplyConfChange -> application completion -> automatic exit proposal rejected by leadTransferee guard -> tickHeartbeat timeout aborts transfer -> service heartbeats and Ready work

supporting_behavior_ids.b-replication: Commit the entry under actual voter quorum; leader proposal guard drops auto-exit during transfer.
supporting_behavior_ids.b-persistence: Ready persistence and completion ordering makes application callback and transfer overlap explicit.
supporting_behavior_ids.b-api: Public serialized calls permit transfer between commitment and completion without concurrent RawNode access.
supporting_behavior_ids.b-election: A new leader provides an alternative retry through its initial entry; the selected history retains the same leader.

counterevidence: appliedTo retries on every later application callback, and a newly elected leader appends an empty entry that can supply such progress.
Transfer success may move responsibility to a new leader; therefore an unavailable transfer target with continued quorum is needed.
Ordinary application proposals are allowed to be dropped; automatic exit ownership is separately assigned to Raft by the JointImplicit/AutoLeave interface.

The existing TestRawNodeJointAutoLeave covers leadership loss followed by renewed campaign and application, not transfer timeout with an idle continuing leader. Its final ApplyConfChange explicitly pretends uncommitted work applied and cannot be reused as a legal prefix.
unknowns: The finite exploration establishes idle retention, not an arbitrary contractual deadline. A fixed check must expose the drained state and a repeatable timer/message cycle, with source correspondence establishing whether any protocol-driven exit trigger remains.
Broader availability consequences for changing voter sets are outside the explored learner-addition history.
question.trigger_rationale: Source shows an assigned automatic task and a lost scheduling trigger: appliedTo submits the exit, transfer guard drops it, and timeout only clears leadTransferee. This has a clearer contract than postponed-read loss (explicitly permitted with retries), and a smaller controlled history than the disputed README persistence overlap. Execute a legal prefix with continued quorum and a no-transfer control to distinguish hidden retry work from an idle stuck joint configuration.

obligation.description: When Raft owns automatic exit from an applied implicit joint configuration, temporary rejection of its exit proposal during leadership transfer must not leave the automatic transition dependent on an unrelated application proposal after that transfer aborts. A continuing eligible leader with a responsive joint quorum and completed preceding application must retain or regenerate protocol-driven work that can propose and complete the exit.

scope.description: Automatic exit continuation on a stable continuing leader after transfer timeout, with the joint change committed and applied, previous persistence/application drained, a responsive quorum in both voter sets, and no new application proposals required for automatic progress.
assumptions: Non-Byzantine messages originate from actual nodes.
Caller serializes RawNode operations, persists before messages, applies committed configuration in order, and advances after application.
Leader remains eligible; live voter quorum processes messages and ticks; transfer target can remain unavailable.
excluded: An arbitrary numeric tick deadline for general eventual liveness.
Guarantees while quorum is unavailable or caller withholds required storage/application completion.
Safety violations, client-visible outages, or all possible configuration shapes.

pending: Finite execution alone cannot prove permanent nonprogress; correspondence must establish whether observed drained state and repeatable scheduling leave any automatic exit-producing path enabled.

grounding.derivation: raft.proto assigns implicit exit to Raft by automatically proposing a zero configuration change, distinguishes it from application-owned explicit exit, and states AutoLeave transitions when safe. tracker.Config repeats the responsibility when possible. Thus unrelated user traffic cannot be the sole wakeup once transfer obstruction is gone and application/quorum prerequisites remain satisfied. No exact tick deadline is derived. appliedTo and tickHeartbeat locate the loss/retry boundary; their implementation does not itself establish the obligation.
grounding.applicability: Applied JointImplicit/AutoLeave under completed caller duties and continued leader/quorum, including temporary transfer rejection.
unresolved: A fixed observation must distinguish a recurring closed idle execution from a finite scheduling delay.
alternatives: Successful transfer or reelection supplies another leader/application event.
Later user proposal can wake the current implementation, but requiring it would transfer the explicitly automatic responsibility to the application.

feedback.answered: Exploration completed actual quorum commitment at index 3, application during transfer to node 3, transfer timeout by tick 10, and 30 heartbeat responses from live voter 2 with unchanged term 2 and leader role. At ticks 10/20/30 the transfer case retained AutoLeave, three outgoing voters, last=commit=applied=3, zero exit entries and no Ready/network queue. The control appended/applied exit index 4 before ticks; a later ordinary proposal woke the transfer case and led to exit index 5. These are exploratory observations, not formal Evidence or a finite-time violation oracle.
